findings: Minor, a missing standing hypothesis (l.465, l.495, l.504, l.717). The setting of § 6 (l.465: « Σ is a compact connected N-manifold with boundary ∂Σ = ⊔_{j=1}^n B_j ») and thm:upper-bound (l.495) do not say n ≥ 1. For n = 0, a flat T³ satisfies every hypothesis of thm:upper-bound: σ(T³) = 0 ≤ 0, R ≡ 0 is constant, and an empty boundary is minimal and has no B_j to be round. thm:upper-bound itself holds (Y = 0 ≤ 0 = −inf F). cor:negative fails: F_g(1) = 0 because there is no boundary term, so inf F_g = 0, Y_[g](Σ) = 0, and R_g ≡ 0 is scalar flat. The proof (l.728) uses lem:positivity, whose statement (l.717) asks for « non-empty boundary ». Model counterexample: Yamabe.toyClosed_counterexample. On the closed two-point model (n = 0) with R ≡ 0 it proves a GluingInput with β = c_N and y = 0, minimal boundary, vol ≠ 0, measurable densities, and also inf F = 0, Y = 0 and R ≡ 0. The flat-T³ instance is argued, not formalized. Suggested fix: state n ≥ 1 at l.465 or in cor:negative. The « punctured torus » sentence (l.504) is not affected, because a punctured torus has n ≥ 1.
questions: « In particular a Schwarzschild-like punctured torus is never scalar flat » (l.504). Reading taken, as the planner proposed: ¬ ∀ x, R_g x = 0 under thm:upper-bound's hypotheses as the model reads them (the last conjunct of cor_negative). The torus Σ̄ = T³, the radii r_j and the roundness of the B_j are not modelled. That such a metric satisfies thm:upper-bound's hypotheses is argued, not formalized: σ(T³) ≤ 0 because T³ carries no metric of positive scalar curvature (MR569070); round spheres are conformally round; N = 3. That argument is the content of « in particular ». Is this reading acceptable?

« Under the hypotheses of Theorem thm:upper-bound, inf F_g > 0 » (l.504). Reading taken: this assertion is lem:positivity (l.717). It holds for every metric on a compact connected Σ with ∂Σ ≠ ∅, independently of thm:upper-bound's other hypotheses. It is carried (hpos), so cor_negative's first conjunct is its hypothesis restated, and the row cannot be closed before lem:positivity is (T-yamabe-scope).

« R_g < 0 » (l.504). Reading taken: R_g ≡ c pointwise and c < 0 (hence R_g x < 0 for every x). The identity R_g = Y_[g](Σ) Vol(Σ, g)^{−2/N} of l.728 is a further conjunct. The hypotheses of thm:upper-bound are taken in the _of_pos reading of T-yamabe-gluing-algebra (no R_g ≤ 0, which l.724 takes from prop:nonpositive). The reading with R_g ≤ 0 carried (upper_bound_of_gluings) would also need lem:positivity for c < 0.

questions: Which form of lem:kobayashi (b) is carried. Reading taken: only its conclusion for the metric g of the statement (KobayashiB g), with min_Σ R_g read ⨅ x, R_g x as in the strict CurvedMetric.kobM. Carrying it for every metric would be stronger than the proof needs.

« R_g ≤ 0 » (l.478). Reading taken: pointwise, ∀ x, R_g x ≤ 0. On an empty Σ this is vacuous and EH = Y = 0, so no nonemptiness is assumed. « Constant scalar curvature » is read pointwise, as in T-yamabe-gluing-algebra. The pointwise reading is needed: if R_g = c held only a.e., (b)'s premise ⨅ R_g > 0 could fail on a null set even for c > 0, and (b) would not exclude c > 0.

The proof's « Lemma kobayashi(b) excludes R_g > 0 » (l.645) is read as: R_g ≡ c > 0 gives min_Σ R_g = c > 0, so (b) gives Y > 0, contradicting the first sentence. This is fact (iii) (l.334), direction « Y ≤ 0 ⇒ R_g ≤ 0 », which the paper also attributes to lem:kobayashi.

kb_proposals: A GluingInput with β_j = c_N exists on the two-point toy model once R_g is negative enough. The body's H absorbs the conformal law and the cap's H the boundary Yamabe inequality (YamabeScaffold.Negative: toyNegInput, with R_g ≡ −8, u = 1, y = 0, H_h ≡ −4, H_{D_0} ≡ 4, EHB(D_0) = 16 ≥ c_3). toyCurved (R ≡ −1) admits none (toyCurved_no_gluingInput), so the input is a genuine restriction and a witness for an upper-bound assembly must pick its metric.

Exact norms on the two-point toy model (T-yamabe-negative): toy_dirichlet (2(a−b)²), toy_normSq_bvol (b² on the boundary point, for any q > 0), toy_normSq_vol_eq (((a²)³ + (b²)³)^{1/3}) and toy_normSq_vol_le (≤ a² + b²). With them, lem:positivity (toy_two_le_infF: inf F ≥ 2) and lem:kobayashi (b) (toy_kobayashiB) are provable on the toy model. c_3 ∈ [12, 16] is cN_three_ge, cN_three_le.

A MeasuredModel with n = 0 (μb := Fin.elim0, each per-boundary field fun j => j.elim0) is a cheap closed Σ. On it F(1) = 0, so inf F = 0 (toyClosed_infF), and the empty Filling gives a GluingInput for free (toyClosedInput). Use it to test whether a statement needs ∂Σ ≠ ∅.
